text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: LATENCY ALERT: observed sudden p50/p95 increase for /v1/generate in us-west-2, starting ~1794999900. p50 up from 120ms -> 260ms, p95 up from 420ms -> 1.2s. Error rate stable. Paging oncall.
oncall-sre: I'm on it. Linking dashboards and traces — https://dashboards.internal/redwood/latency?svc=runtime (private). Anyone on-call for eng-runtime?
alex: i can join for kernel/perf traces, pinging @eng-runtime. Oncall, what's the impact — any large customers seeing errors or just increased latency?
product-ops: several high-throughput customers reported slow UI responses, support tickets opened, one customer (acct: acme-analytics) seeing timeouts at 30s on long prompts. We should notify CSMs if impact persists.
maya: running quick check: host-level CPU shows steal ~0. No large I/O. Network egress looks normal. But observed context-switch rates spiking on a subset of machines.
samir: adding quick trace span summary from a sampled request: span distribution indicates much more time in "kernel-sched" and "gpu-queue-wait" than usual. Attaching snippet.

julia: copy of sampled trace spans (trimmed):
```
root -> parse -> tokenize -> model-infer
model-infer:
  - kv-lookup: 12ms (normal)
  - forward-kernel: 30ms (norm)
  - gpu-queue-wait: 180ms (was ~10ms)
  - kernel-sched: 110ms (was ~3ms)
```

alex: hmm GPU queue wait up massively. Could be driver/kernel scheduling or host-side CPU starvation. Anyone recently rolled a kernel or changed cgroup configs in us-west-2?
eng-runtime: we rolled kernel 6.2.18 -> 6.3.1 on a handful of nodes in the cluster as part of security backports at ~1794999000. We also deployed a new CUDA driver minor rev yesterday.
perf-bot: perf counters snapshot for a representative host:
```
cpu-cycles: 1.2e11
context-switches: 1.9e6 (baseline ~2e5)
softirqs: elevated
irq/softirq wait: higher
```

oncall-sre: hypothesis list (live):
- H1: kernel change altered scheduler behaviour leading to increased context switches and GPU queue delays.
- H2: CUDA driver micro-change interacts with runtime kernel module causing queue backpressure.
- H3: a runtime release changed batch scheduling (but releases show no traffic-weighted rollout here).

samir: I'm starting a narrow rollback plan on a small canary pool (10%) to kernel 6.2.18 on a few nodes. If latency improves we'll escalate rollback. I'll post results in 5m.
alex: while rollback runs, please capture bpftrace stack traces and collect dmesg + NVME logs. bpftrace one-liner to watch wakeups by pid:
```
bpftrace -e 'tracepoint:sched:sched_wakeup /comm == "redwood-runtime"/ { @[comm] = count(); }'
```

julia: collecting dmesg now; saw repeated messages like:
```
[1794999952.123] task redwood-runtime invoked resched while in atomic
[1794999953.456] GPU driver: stall detected on queue 3
```

product-ops: CSMs notified for top 5 affected customers. We recommended temporary route to fallback-small model for latency-sensitive paths.
oncall-sre: rollback patch applied to canary nodes at 1795000300. Monitoring latencies...

perf-bot: canary latency p50 -> dropped from 270ms to 130ms within 90s after rollback. p95 down from 1.1s -> 450ms. Non-canary remains high.

oncall-sre: early signal points to H1 (kernel change). Need broader rollback? eng-runtime, what's the risk to expand rollback to full AZ?
eng-runtime: expanding rollback requires node reboots; we can do a phased rollback per-host. Request approval: risk of transient evictions and token expiration. Product-ops: approve for us-west-2 to restore customer experience.

alex: parallel ask: gather perf top while under load, and run `nvidia-smi dmon` to see driver queue depths. Also capture `cat /proc/sched_debug` pre/post if possible.
maya: running nvidia-smi dmon on a canary host now — showing large GPU utilization but several processes in 'pending' state.

samir: full AZ rollback started at 1795000500. Will post progress. Ops: expect short evictions, notify customers.

perf-bot: after AZ-wide rollback p50/p95 returned to baseline within 6 minutes. Host perf counters back to normal, context-switches down to baseline. Trend suggests kernel scheduler change was primary cause.

oncall-sre: ACTIONS (in-incident RCA tracking):
- Collect list of hosts that received kernel 6.3.1 and CUDA driver revs (samir)
- Upload full perf counter dumps and trace IDs to incident folder (alex)
- Draft customer impact timeline and notify CSMs (product-ops)
- Postmortem to include root cause, rollback timeline, and mitigation (julia)

alex: uploading logs to /incidents/1795000123/logs (internal). Link: https://internal.files/incidents/1795000123/logs.tar.gz

julia: quick timeline for postmortem notes:
```
1794999000 - security kernel rollout started (6.3.1)
1794999900 - customer reports + automated alert: p50/p95 drift
1795000123 - incident channel opened (this thread)
1795000300 - canary rollback -> latency improves
1795000500 - AZ rollback started
1795000660 - latency restored to baseline
```

product-ops: CSMs informed; we offered mitigation steps to customers (route to fallback-small model, retry policy). No data loss.

eng-runtime: follow-ups:
- Reproduce kernel scheduler regression in a lab with 6.3.1 under similar workload and GPU driver combination.
- Coordinate with infra/kernel team to file CVE/backport notes if needed.
- Add automated canary to detect p95 spikes after kernel updates (hook into deploy pipeline).

oncall-sre: closing incident channel after handoff to postmortem owners. Tagging postmortem leads: julia (ops), alex (perf), eng-runtime.

julia: I'll start the RCA doc and include the hypotheses above, the perf dumps, and commands we used. Thanks everyone for quick response. :clap:

samir: leaving note for the postmortem: consider gating kernel rollouts when high-latency-sensitive workloads are present; add test that stresses scheduler with many short-lived threads.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: status -> mitigated. Duration 00:12:37. Tickets linked: INC-5532.
